title: Build a tiny backward-walking engine
brief: Write the two-sided slope check, the multiply rule, and the backward walk, then confirm them on c = a*b + a and on a diamond.
hints: central_difference is one line: (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2 * h).

In __mul__, the slope that reaches self is out.grad times other.value, and the slope that reaches other is out.grad times self.value. Use += for both, because a * a puts the same tensor in both places.
In backward, build the order with a depth-first walk that appends a node only after all of its children have been appended, and keep a visited set of id(node) so a shared node is appended once.
After the order is built, set self.grad to ones and call _backward_fn on every node in reversed order.
